memos.headline: Momentum Bifurcation: GOOGL and CAT Overbought Near Highs While PG and UNH Lag Badly
memos.body: I see a clear split in this universe between parabolic leaders and broken laggards. GOOGL and CAT are the standout momentum names—both up 43% and 38% over 12 weeks respectively with massive relative strength vs SPY—but RSIs of 77 and 74 plus extreme extensions above the 50-day mean (15% and 21%) warn of near-term mean-reversion risk. AMZN just printed a fresh 52-week high with a healthier RSI of 67 and strong 4-week relative strength of +9.3%, making it the cleanest trend-following setup. On the other side, PG sits 16% off its high, below both moving averages, with persistent negative relative strength, and UNH is a structural wreck at -45% from its 52-week high despite a sharp 12-week bounce—its RSI of 40 and renewed weekly selling suggest the bounce is fading. I'd ride AMZN and AAPL on trend, wait for GOOGL/CAT to pull back before adding, and avoid PG and UNH until they reclaim their 50-day means.

views.note: Fresh 52-week high, RSI 67 not yet overbought, +9.3% 4w relative strength vs SPY; would reassess on a close below 225 (roughly the 50d mean area).
Within 0.4% of 52-week high, +15% 12w relative strength, RSI 69 approaching but not yet overbought; a close below 248 (50d mean zone) would change my view.
Extraordinary 12w +43% run and +35% relative strength, but RSI 77 and 15% above 50d mean signal overextension; I'd wait for a pullback toward 245 before getting long.
RSI 74 and a staggering 21% above the 50d mean after +88% in 26 weeks—trend is powerful but stretched; need a consolidation toward 480 to get involved.
Up 86% over 26 weeks, 11% above 50d mean with RSI 67; trend is intact and relative strength positive, but volatility (ATR 3%) demands tight sizing; invalidated below 182.
Flat 12-week return, negative relative strength vs SPY (-8.5% over 12w), RSI 48—no directional edge; needs to break above 540 or I stay sidelined.
Down 16% from high, below both 50d and 200d means, persistent negative relative strength (-10% over 12w); would reconsider only on a close above 154 (50d mean).
Still 45% off its 52-week high, below the 200d mean by 12%, RSI 40 and falling 6% last week—structurally damaged; no entry until a sustained close above 370.
Healthy 26w return of +28% but 4w relative strength is -1.6% and RSI 59 is middling; trend is fine but not leading—hold, don't add.
Flat relative strength, only 4% above 200d mean, RSI 52—dead money with no catalyst in the tape; needs a breakout above 122 to get interesting.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Lead on Earnings Power; UNH Margin Collapse and XOM Earnings Decline Flash Warning Signs
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in NVDA (+55.6% YoY revenue, 56.5% net margin) and GOOGL (+15.9% revenue, 34.2% margin with net income up 33%), both filed within the last two months. MSFT's freshly filed Q1 FY2026 shows 18.4% revenue growth and a 35.7% net margin on minimal leverage ($43.2B debt), reinforcing its position as a compounding machine. On the other side, UNH's Q3 is alarming: despite 12.2% revenue growth, net income collapsed 61.2% YoY to just $2.35B on $113B of revenue, compressing the net margin to 2.1%—I need to see whether medical cost ratios stabilize before getting constructive. XOM and CAT are both showing revenue and earnings declines in a softening macro, and JPM's Q2 revenue fell 10.5% YoY with net income down 17.4%, though its 33.4% margin still reflects strong banking profitability. I would change my view on UNH if net margin recovers above 5% and on XOM if commodity prices firm enough to reverse the earnings trajectory.

views.note: 56.5% net margin and 55.6% YoY revenue growth with only $8.5B total debt represent extraordinary earnings power and balance sheet strength.
Revenue up 15.9% and net income up 33% YoY to $35B on a 34.2% margin with just $14.8B debt is a compelling earnings acceleration story.
18.4% revenue growth, 35.7% net margin, and moderate $43.2B debt make this a high-quality compounder, though net income growth of 12.5% lagging revenue growth bears monitoring.
Net income surged 34.7% YoY on 13.3% revenue growth, pushing margin to 10.8%, but I want to see margin durability above 10% in subsequent quarters before raising conviction.
Solid 24.9% margin and 9.6% revenue growth, but $91.8B in total debt is the highest in the universe and top-line growth is the slowest among mega-cap tech peers.
Net income up 20% YoY on only 3% revenue growth signals margin expansion, but low top-line growth limits upside; I'd need organic volume acceleration to get more constructive.
Revenue down 10.5% and net income down 17.4% YoY are concerning, though a 33.4% net margin shows the franchise is still highly profitable; need Q3 data to assess trajectory.
Net income down 61.2% YoY with net margin compressing to just 2.1% on $80.1B debt signals severe cash-flow compression that I refuse to pay for until margin stabilizes above 5%.
Revenue down 12.4% and net income down 23.4% YoY with an 8.7% margin reflect commodity headwinds eroding earnings power; would revisit if energy prices recover.
Flat revenue (-0.7%) and an 18.7% decline in net income suggest a cyclical downturn is compressing earnings, and $31.7B in debt relative to $16.6B quarterly revenue adds risk.

memos.headline: Fed Easing Cycle Meets Sticky Inflation and Rising Unemployment — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Fade Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound has dropped 100bp over 12 months to 4.00%, with 50bp of that in the last three months alone, while the 10y yield has declined 26bp over the same three months to 4.11%. However, the macro backdrop is not clean — CPI is running at 3.0% YoY and unemployment has risen 30bp over three months to 4.40%, signaling a softening labor market that could tip toward outright slowdown. The curve has re-steepened meaningfully (+36bp YoY on the 10y-2y spread to +0.50pp), consistent with markets pricing further front-end cuts but some term premium for persistent inflation. I have conviction that this easing-into-slowdown regime favors long-duration growth names and defensive staples over cyclicals and energy; a November CPI print above 3.2% YoY or a payrolls miss pushing unemployment above 4.6% would force me to reassess toward a stagflation call.

views.note: Falling front-end rates and declining 10y yields directly support long-duration growth equities with recurring revenue; MSFT benefits from easing without cyclical exposure.
Duration tailwind from rate cuts supports premium consumer tech, though rising unemployment at 4.40% is a modest headwind to discretionary hardware spend.
Defensive staples outperform in a slowdown regime with unemployment trending higher; PG's pricing power also provides a hedge against 3% CPI.
Steeper curve (+50bp 10y-2y) supports NIM, but rising unemployment and slowing economy raise credit loss concerns — offsetting forces keep me neutral.
Cyclical industrials face headwinds from rising unemployment and a softening economy; 30bp increase in jobless rate over 3 months signals weakening capex demand.
Energy typically underperforms in easing-into-slowdown regimes as demand expectations weaken alongside rising unemployment.
Secular AI demand plus falling discount rates from 100bp of cumulative cuts make NVDA attractive on a duration basis despite elevated valuations.
Easing cycle benefits both the consumer discretionary and cloud segments; however, 3% CPI and 4.4% unemployment inject some uncertainty on consumer spending.
Ad revenue is cyclically sensitive and a slowdown regime tempers my enthusiasm despite the duration tailwind from lower rates.
Defensive healthcare is typically a slowdown beneficiary, but regulatory and political uncertainty keeps conviction low at the macro level.

memos.headline: AMZN and CAT Post-Earnings Sentiment Surges Stand Out; MSFT Reaction Flags Caution
memos.body: I am reading the post-earnings price reactions across the universe as the clearest sentiment signal this week. AMZN's +9.6% move on its 10/30 results filing and CAT's +11.6% pop on 10/29 indicate strongly positive narrative shifts—these are outsized reactions that suggest the market was positioned too cautiously heading in. MSFT's -2.9% drop after its 10/29 results filing is a negative tone shift worth monitoring, especially given the prior officer departure filing on 9/30 that may have seeded uncertainty. AAPL's muted -0.4% reaction to its 10/30 earnings filing suggests the result was largely priced and sentiment is neutral. JPM's -1.9% post-earnings reaction on 10/14 and subsequent 8-K filings have not generated a clear recovery narrative, leaving me cautious there.

views.note: A +9.6% post-earnings move signals a decisive positive sentiment shift that likely has room to carry as analysts revise estimates upward.
An +11.6% earnings-day surge reflects a major positive narrative reset for an industrial bellwether, suggesting prior positioning was too bearish.
The -2.9% post-earnings decline combined with a recent officer departure filing suggests negative sentiment momentum that may not yet be fully absorbed.
A -0.4% post-earnings move is essentially flat, indicating the result was in-line and sentiment is balanced with no clear directional edge.
A +2.5% post-earnings reaction is modestly positive and suggests constructive sentiment, though the move is not outsized enough for high conviction.
The -1.9% earnings reaction on 10/14 and subsequent filings have not catalyzed a positive tone reversal, leaving sentiment tepid.
A +0.2% post-earnings move is a non-event from a sentiment perspective; multiple Reg FD filings suggest management is actively managing narrative but the market is unmoved.
A +0.5% post-earnings reaction is mildly positive but not enough to signal a meaningful sentiment shift given the stock's recent headline risk.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing but Oil Weakness and Elevated VIX Signal Unresolved Geopolitical Crosscurrents
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has dropped 31% over the past month to 280, yet remains elevated on a 3-month basis (+2.1%), suggesting that while acute trade-policy fears may have receded, structural uncertainty around export controls and China policy persists. WTI crude at $61.36 is down nearly 14% over three months, which I read as a demand-side signal consistent with slowing global activity and possibly reduced geopolitical risk premium on energy supply—a headwind for XOM but a tailwind for cost-sensitive industrials and consumer staples. VIX at 16.91 is creeping higher (+9.2% over 3 months), and HY spreads have barely moved, so credit markets are not yet pricing a hard landing but are watchful. I have moderate conviction that NVDA and AAPL remain most exposed to any re-escalation of semiconductor export controls or China supply-chain disruption, while domestically oriented names like UNH and JPM carry less geopolitical tail risk. A material change in my view would come from new semiconductor export restrictions, a reversal in the EPU trend, or a supply-driven oil spike above $75.

views.note: Most exposed to potential tightening of AI-chip export controls to China; structural risk persists even as near-term EPU eases.
China manufacturing concentration remains a structural vulnerability, but no new policy trigger evident in current data.
WTI down 14% over 3 months to $61.36 reflects weak demand and reduced geopolitical supply premium, pressuring upstream margins.
Domestically oriented with limited direct geopolitical exposure; steepening yield curve over 3 months (+6bp) supports net interest income.
Purely domestic healthcare demand insulates from trade and export-control risks; regulatory uncertainty is the main watch item.
Lower oil prices help input costs, but global consumer exposure means FX and trade-policy shifts could swing margins either way.
Benefits from infrastructure spending but exposed to global capex slowdown implied by falling oil; recent Reg FD filing warrants monitoring.

plan.summary: Overweight high-quality growth names benefiting from the Fed easing cycle and strong earnings momentum, led by AMZN (broadest analyst agreement) and NVDA (exceptional fundamentals). Maintain meaningful cash buffer (~25%) given elevated policy uncertainty, overbought conditions in some names, and rising unemployment signaling potential slowdown.

plans.changes_my_mind: New semiconductor export restrictions announced targeting China AI chips, or a close below 182 invalidating the technical trend.

plans.rationale: Fundamentals strongly supportive (revenue +15.9%, net income +33%, 34.2% margin) and Sentiment modestly positive (+2.5% post-earnings). plans.changes_my_mind: RSI expansion above 80 with a failed breakout reversal, or a close below 245 confirming mean-reversion has begun.
